samples.summary: ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard fails open when `req.user` is absent, so its whole effect depends on mount order — and the new folders guard-order test only pins CombinedAuthGuard before WorkspaceScopeGuard, not before the write-scope guard
samples.evidence: `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard.canActivate` reads `request.user` and returns `true` unconditionally when it is falsy (`if (!user?.isApiKey) return true;`, api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:44). That is safe only because `CombinedAuthGuard` is listed first in `@UseGuards(CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard)` (folders.controller.ts:39) and therefore populates `req.user` first. If the guard list is ever reordered so the write-scope guard runs before authentication, `req.user` is `undefined`, the guard returns `true`, authentication then succeeds, and a `scopes: ['read']` API key can POST/PATCH/DELETE every v1 route — the exact class of hole the guard was written to close (see its own doc comment about `PUT /content`). The delta this round strengthens the folders guard spec but its ordering assertion (folders.controller.spec.ts:35-39) compares only `CombinedAuthGuard` vs `WorkspaceScopeGuard`; nothing anywhere asserts `CombinedAuthGuard` precedes `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard`. A closed form (`if (!user) throw`/deny, or asserting the ordering) would remove the dependence on list order.

samples.summary: The "is mounted on every v1 controller" regression test enumerates 7 of the 14 v1 controllers, leaving the seven worksheet-* controllers' write-scope mounting unasserted
samples.evidence: The folders spec touched by this delta states that mounting is itself the security boundary (folders.controller.spec.ts:11-16), and the sibling spec claims to enforce that for the whole surface: `describe('is mounted on every v1 controller')` (api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78) lists docs-content, documents, files, folders, images, tabs, cells. `Grep '@UseGuards' packages/backend/src/api/v1` shows seven more controllers with mutating routes — worksheet, worksheet-rules, worksheet-filter-pivot, worksheet-styles, worksheet-dimensions, worksheet-charts, worksheet-structure — that mount the guard today but are not in the list. Removing `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` from, e.g., worksheet-structure.controller.ts:63 (row/column deletes) would let a read-only API key mutate sheet data with no test failing, while the test name reads as full coverage. Not exploitable as written; the enumeration is simply incomplete.
